title: It looks like the Atlantic storm season may finally produce a hurricane
gist: The 2026 Atlantic season has not yet produced a hurricane, an unprecedented situation in the modern record; a Gulf low that could become Isaias has a decent chance of becoming a hurricane and a landfall between southeastern Louisiana and the Florida Panhandle later this week.

insights.claim: No Atlantic season in the modern record (about WWII onward) has been without a hurricane, and none has gone this late in the year without one forming.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A hurricane-free season is historically anomalous, relevant for catastrophe and insurance loss expectations.
insights.locator: Normally, a hurricane forming in early October

insights.claim: A strengthening El Niño expected to become historically strong is producing wind shear over the tropical Atlantic that has made this the quietest season to date by most metrics.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: El Niño is the driver of suppressed storm activity.
insights.locator: The Atlantic tropics have been exceptionally quiet

insights.claim: Most hurricanes form between mid-August and mid-October, so the window for the season's first hurricane is closing.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Limited remaining time lowers the odds of further storms.

insights.claim: A Gulf of Mexico low expected to be named Isaias could strengthen into a hurricane, with some model guidance suggesting a major hurricane, helped by central Gulf waters of 28-30 C that are well above normal.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Warm water gives intensification potential; Gulf energy, ports and insurers should monitor.

insights.claim: Most model guidance points to landfall between southeastern Louisiana and the Florida Panhandle on Friday or Saturday, with heavy rain certain but wind and storm surge threats depending on how well organized the storm becomes.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Gulf Coast landfall zone covers energy infrastructure and ports.
